text:
samir: Quick ping — I opened PR 1234 that tightens the auth scopes on the VPC egress proxy and swaps the SA used by onprem connectors. Would like a security + infra quick-pass before I merge in the morning. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1234 :eyes:

olivia: taking a look now. main concerns: (1) does this change broaden any secrets access? (2) any cross-region KMS implications?

samir: good q — it narrows the SA role for the connector (removes iam:List* and broad storage access), but it adds a new conditional binding to allow key access from the connector's VPC subnet. I added comments in the PR explaining why.

jess: can you paste the exact diff for the IAM binding? I want to verify there isn't a wildcard resource.

samir: sure — snippet from iam.yaml in the PR:

```yaml
- members:
-   - serviceAccount:connectors@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- role: roles/storage.admin
+ members:
+   - serviceAccount:connectors@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+ role: roles/storage.objectViewer
+ condition:
+   title: "restrict_to_vpc"
+   expression: "resource.name.startsWith(\"projects/_/subnetworks/rdw-vpc/\")"
```

rene: hmm that condition looks fine but double-check the expression — Cloud IAM conditions don't accept resource.name like that in all contexts. Did you validate with `gcloud iam roles` dry-run?

samir: I ran `gcloud iam roles describe` and a local validate script — infra-bot also ran the Terraform plan. The plan shows the condition as an "expr" in the binding.

infra-bot: PLAN: 1 to add, 1 to change. No resources will be destroyed. Potential diff flagged for Cloud KMS cryptoKey.iampolicy change.

olivia: thanks infra-bot. Samir — KMS note: the change grants the connector SA access to decrypt for a single key but the binding references the key by name, not by location. Can you make sure the key resource is fully qualified (projects/PROJECT/locations/LOCATION/keyRings/NAME/cryptoKeys/KEY)?

samir: yep good catch, updated the PR to use full resource path. also added a test case showing the connector token cannot list buckets.

jess: can security review confirm if this is acceptable for Private deployments (onprem) where customers may have stricter SA scoping? We need a short checklist to include in the PR description.

olivia: from a sec POV: - no wildcard roles left, - condition tied to VPC is good but brittle across subnet renames, - key is fully qualified now. Approve pending a short note in the PR about how to update the condition when a customer renames subnets.

rene: +1, also ask infra to run the integration that simulates a connector in a different VPC to ensure the condition blocks correctly.

samir: noted. @infra-bot can you queue the vpc-sim job?

infra-bot: Job queued: vpc-sim-connector-test (ETA ~8m).

security-bot: Quick reminder — any changes touching KMS keys must include a key rotation plan and the key policy audit checklist link: https://go/redwood/kms-audit. Please add that to PR 1234 before merge.

samir: added a section in the PR with rotation plan + link to checklist. Also added a merge freeze window note: will wait for infra test + one more security ack, aiming to merge between 09:00-10:00 PT tomorrow.

jess: sounds good. thanks for doing the limited-scope change instead of broad role swap. :thumbsup:

olivia: I can give the final 👍 after infra test passes and you add the checklist link (thanks).

samir: thanks everyone — will follow up here once infra job finishes. :pray:

[integration note: infra job completed successfully at ~2475012700 — infra-bot]

infra-bot: vpc-sim-connector-test: SUCCESS. No policy violations detected.

samir: merging now per agreed window — will monitor. cc @jess @olivia

jess: :rocket: thanks for the clear thread.

olivia: monitoring logs for the key access after merge.

security-bot: Post-merge checklist reminder: update audit ticket #SEC-789 and mark key policy reviewed.

samir: done, ticket updated. closing thread.
